chapter: Cotton Club and radio fame with Cab
title: The Cotton Club: gangsters, Walter Winchell and George Raft
summary: He recalls tiring of 'Minnie the Moocher' for Winchell, Owney Madden's ownership with Herman Stark as front man, and George Raft dancing to 'Sweet Georgia Brown'.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So now the band is Cab Calloway's band. What happens now? What year was that?
That was in the Thirties, I guess. '31... Maybe it was '30.
Did you make that trip to Europe with them?

Yeah. It's whenever Duke went to make Three Little Words. That's when we got our break. Because we went to the Cotton Club, and we had all that air time. And man, we got so sick of playing "Minnie The Moocher"... One guy used to come in the club, and if we had already played it, we had to play it again for him -- Walter Winchell. Somehow he'd get mad when he'd come in. Even though he'd come in at 10:30 or 11 o'clock, and we'd already played "Minnie The Moocher."
Now, this is the Cotton Club.
Yeah.
The Cotton Club was a ...(?)... along with the men of note of New York into the underworld. Right?
Yes.
It was owned by the Underworld.
Owney Madden.
Thomas - 97
Owney Madden. And...

The gangsters owned it. And they had a guy in charge of it, Herman Stark... He was a kind of bragging(?) guy, but he didn't have no record against him. So he could be the... He was the front man. He was the Man.
Foots, Remember when we had guys like George Raft that used to come in?
Yeah. George Raft used to come in. And George Raft was a...
What would we have to play for them, Foots?
'Sweet Georgia Brown.' And he'd get on the floor and do his dance to "Sweet Georgia Brown," and we was like an idol of his, because we knew him when he was... See, George Raft was never a gangster.
No.
The gangsters just liked him.
He was one of the boys.

He was one of the boys. And he was a kind of gigolo, too. Because George Raft sometimes would come in with some beautiful woman, he'd just escort to the Cotton Club and escort her back home. And he was a handsome guy, and he could dance.
Now, he just died, just recently.
Yeah, right. Yeah, we followed his career.
